picks.intervention_label: Confirmatory workup: validated GIS (Myriad MyChoice CDx) + HER2 re-stain
picks.rationale: The patient ranked this herself: "treat its confirmatory assay as the rank-1 shared workup." Her germline and somatic BRCA already read wild-type, so the question still open is a validated MyChoice CDx GIS, and a result of >=42 is the single gate that unlocks the highest-magnitude maintenance on the board (olaparib + bevacizumab). I would run a confirmatory HER2 re-stain in the same sitting, since the new HER2-low 1+ call rests on one surgical-path specimen and Altera could not read HER2 at all. No toxicity, no modality conflict, and it decides which of the options below are even live.
primary_concerns: Honors her stated rank-1 shared workup; somatic and germline BRCA already resolved wild-type, so the live gate is a validated MyChoice CDx GIS >=42
Single-specimen HER2 1+ basis (Altera could not evaluate HER2); a re-stain hardens whether the HER2-directed options below are real for her
Pure decision-gating: no toxicity, no modality conflict, clears every preference axis

picks.rationale: This is the one maintenance option that clears both of her named vetoes outright: no added peripheral neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression, on a backbone she already tolerates. The honest cost is the ceiling. GOG-218 buys PFS (HR 0.717, 14.1 vs 10.3 mo) with no overall-population survival gain, which sits uneasily against her 0.7 efficacy lean. The live caution is her own: anti-angiogenic VTE and bleeding risk against a high VTE history and a prior IVC filter, which I would handle with BP and bleeding monitoring rather than treat as a stop.
primary_concerns: Clears both named vetoes: no added neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression
Modality tension: VTE and bleeding risk against her high VTE history and prior IVC filter, managed rather than escalated
Efficacy ceiling is PFS-only (HR 0.717) with no OS gain, in tension with her 0.7 efficacy lean
Low-infusion: partial (IV q3w, but she already tolerates it)

picks.rationale: Oral, once daily, no infusion, and it trips none of her vetoes, so for the 70-79 band and her oral preference this is the gentlest thing on the list. The catch is the evidence: a single retrospective ROBINS-I-serious series (60% vs 38.5% recurrence-free at 24 months), not a randomized result, and her PR-negativity likely trims the ER-driven signal. I would hold this as a low-toxicity adjunct or later-line floor, not a substitute for a trial-backed regimen. It earns its place because it costs her almost nothing in tolerability.
primary_concerns: Best oral and age-band fit on the board; clears every veto
Evidence is the weak point: retrospective, non-randomized, ROBINS-I serious
PR-negativity likely trims the ER-driven magnitude

picks.rationale: She is already on this one, which matters: she prefers trials and she is at R0 on this backbone. It works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment, so her MSS, TMB-low status does not foreclose it the way it kills single-agent checkpoint inhibition, and the OVATION 2 OS signal (HR 0.69) is real if immature. The cost against her preferences is the route: intraperitoneal delivery is not the oral or low-infusion option she asked for, and access outside the trial is not guaranteed. Efficacy still rests on a sponsor topline with no published grade 3+ table, so I rank it on immaturity and route, not on any veto.
primary_concerns: Satisfies prefers_trials and she is already on it at R0
Modality conflict: intraperitoneal, not oral or low-infusion
No named veto triggered; immature efficacy (sponsor topline, no published grade 3+ table)

picks.intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), HER2-low, investigational at IHC 1+
picks.rationale: The new HER2-low axis gives her a HER2-directed option that, unlike disitamab vedotin, clears both of her named vetoes: T-DXd's headline toxicities are ILD and nausea, not peripheral neuropathy or febrile neutropenia. Two real costs keep it here rather than higher. It is IV every three weeks against her low-infusion preference, and for an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor it is investigational, since the tumor-agnostic approval needs 3+ and the supporting signal is extrapolated from HER2-low breast (DESTINY-Breast04/06). Her 1+ also rests on a single specimen, so I would want the rank-1 re-stain to confirm before committing, ideally on a HER2 solid-tumor basket trial.
primary_concerns: Clears both named vetoes: ILD and nausea profile, not neuropathy or febrile neutropenia
Modality tension: IV q3w against the low-infusion preference, plus ILD risk
Investigational at IHC 1+ ovarian (tumor-agnostic approval needs 3+); efficacy extrapolated from HER2-low breast
Single-specimen HER2 basis; confirm with the rank-1 re-stain

picks.rationale: For a patient who leans efficacy at 0.7, this is the strongest oral maintenance on the board: ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52 (20.2 vs 9.2 mo), qualifying her BRCA-wild-type tumor with no GIS gate. I rank it below the clean options for one reason: grade 3+ anemia near 29% presses her severe-myelosuppression veto, and her baseline WBC of 3.5 leaves thin reserve. But that veto is hers to lift, not mine to rank past on her behalf, so if she chooses the efficacy with a hematology-supported dose and monitoring plan on file, this moves up. I would put niraparib a step behind it, since thrombocytopenia plus anemia hit the marrow veto harder.
primary_concerns: Strongest oral PFS signal for her 0.7 efficacy lean (ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52)
Presses the severe-myelosuppression veto (grade 3+ anemia ~29%); thin marrow reserve (WBC 3.5)
Veto is hers to lift; moves up with a hematology-supported dose and monitoring plan on file

notes: Two HER2 options changed the board, and they land on opposite sides of her vetoes. T-DXd I can carry for her, because its toxicity profile (ILD, nausea) sidesteps both named vetoes even though it is IV and investigational at 1+. Disitamab vedotin I reject outright: the MMAE payload runs about 68% peripheral neuropathy and grade 3+ neutropenia, which hits both of her vetoes at once, and its only HER2-low efficacy datapoint is an abstract-only, PAM-pathway-selected breast series. Olaparib + bevacizumab stays foreclosed until a GIS >=42 returns, and even then it stacks a PARP marrow hit on bevacizumab's VTE and bleeding risk against her IVC-filter history. The tension worth putting on the record: she leans efficacy at 0.7 but set two hard vetoes, and the strongest-PFS options (the PARPs, the PAOLA-1 combo) are the same ones that press the marrow veto. So I lead with the workup she asked to rank first, then the therapies that respect her vetoes, and I flag the PARP as a genuine upgrade only if she decides to lift her own marrow veto.

picks.rationale: She is already on the bevacizumab backbone, and that is where the guidelines land for an all-comer at this stage. NCCN Ovarian v3.2024 lists bevacizumab maintenance at category 2A with no biomarker gate, and the ESMO 2026 express update keeps bevacizumab for 15 months on the menu for HRD-negative disease. GOG-218 (pmid 22204724) and ICON7 (pmid 22204725) are the anchors here, both phase 3, both with a real PFS signal. The honest caveat: the benefit is PFS, not OS in the overall population, so this buys time rather than cure.
primary_concerns: GOG-218 and ICON7 enrolled all-comers, but the OS gain in ICON7 sat in the high-risk (stage IV / suboptimal) subset; this stage IIIc R0 patient is adjacent to, not inside, that subset.
Bevacizumab's VTE and bleeding risk runs against her documented high VTE history and prior IVC filter, which is the operative caution here rather than her named neuropathy or marrow vetoes.

picks.rationale: If a validated genomic-instability score comes back at or above threshold, this is the highest-category play she has: NCCN Ovarian v3.2024 puts olaparib + bevacizumab at category 1 for HRD-positive disease, and ESMO scores the BRCA/HRD-positive combination on MCBS v2.0. She is already on the bevacizumab half, so it is an add rather than a switch. The catch is the gate: PAOLA-1 (pmid 31851799) concentrates its benefit in HRD-positive tumors defined by Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not clear that bar.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is contingent: she is BRCA wild-type with only a qualitative Altera instability read, so the cat-1 HRD-positive estimand (HR 0.33) does not yet apply, and below a validated GIS >=42 she defaults to the HRD-negative pathway.
Stacking PARP-related anemia on bevacizumab's hypertension and clotting risk is a real load for a patient in her age band with a VTE history and prior IVC filter.

picks.rationale: Niraparib is the cleanest all-comer maintenance option that does not wait on a companion-diagnostic result. NCCN Ovarian v3.2024 lists it at category 2A for patients who received bevacizumab, PRIMA (pmid 31562799) enrolled regardless of BRCA or HRD score, and ESMO gives it an MCBS v2.0 score of 2 in the HRD-negative setting. Two things temper it: the NCCN panel itself flags minimal PARP benefit in HR-proficient tumors, and the toxicity collides with her stated veto.
primary_concerns: Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% (pmid 31562799) trip her severe-myelosuppression veto; the individualized weight/platelet starting dose softens but does not remove that.
Her benefit likely tracks the overall estimand (HR 0.62) rather than the HRD-positive one (HR 0.43), since she is BRCA wild-type with HRD unconfirmed.

picks.rationale: Second all-comer PARP option if niraparib's marrow profile is the sticking point. ATHENA-MONO (pmid 35658487) showed an ITT benefit that held in the HRD-negative stratum, so a BRCA wild-type tumor still qualifies without a BRCA gate, and ESMO scores it on MCBS v2.0 for HRD-negative disease. It is a maintenance PARP like niraparib, so it sits a notch below the bevacizumab-anchored options for this patient rather than ahead of them.
primary_concerns: Anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6% (pmid 35658487) still engage her myelosuppression veto, so a swap from niraparib trades one marrow risk for another.
Transaminase elevations run about 10%; baseline LFTs are normal, but a bilirubin of 1.5 is worth watching.

picks.rationale: Low-burden, oral, and a fit for her stated preference and age band. That is the case for letrozole, not the evidence grade. NCCN lists hormone therapy as an option in this disease, but the maintenance signal here is a non-randomized retrospective series (pmid 29157627), not a phase 3, and her ER-positive (~80%) but PR-negative profile predicts a real-but-modest effect.
primary_concerns: The supporting data is a retrospective comparison nested in a translational study, well below the phase 3 evidence behind the PARP and bevacizumab options.
PR-negativity tempers expected magnitude, so this reads as a tolerability-driven later option rather than a primary maintenance choice.

notes: On the new HER2-low (IHC 1+) finding: I left the HER2-directed options off the ranked list on purpose. There is no NCCN, ESMO, or SGO endorsement for HER2-directed therapy in HER2-low ovarian cancer. The tumor-agnostic trastuzumab deruxtecan approval requires IHC 3+, the DESTINY-PanTumor02 ovarian cohort (pmid 37870536) enrolled IHC 2+/3+, and the IHC 1+ evidence is all breast (DESTINY-Breast04 pmid 35665782, Breast06 pmid 39282896); this is cross-tumor extrapolation she cannot enroll on. Disitamab vedotin baskets (nct NCT06003231, NCT06660511) do accept ovarian IHC 1+, but they are investigational and the MMAE payload carries the neuropathy and neutropenia she has vetoes against. If the board wants to pursue HER2, the guideline-aligned route is a trial, after a confirmatory re-stain, since the current 1+ rests on a single specimen and Altera could not evaluate HER2. For now it sits behind the maintenance decision, which is the actual question in front of us.

picks.rationale: Niraparib carries the longest post-marketing PARP safety record in this setting (recurrent-disease approval 2017, 1L all-comer maintenance 2020), so the toxicity is predictable and the management algorithm is settled. PRIMA's all-comer PFS HR was 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76), the cleanest fit here because enrolment never required a BRCA mutation or a validated GIS, and this tumor has neither. The catch is her myelosuppression veto: G3+ anemia 31%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%, against a baseline WBC already at 3.5. I rank it first only with an individualized starting dose, which lowered G3+ thrombocytopenia in PRIMA, plus serial CBCs and dose holds; absent that gating I would veto.
primary_concerns: Triggers the severe-myelosuppression/febrile-neutropenia veto; the rank is conditional on an individualized starting dose and serial CBC monitoring
Baseline WBC 3.5 leaves little marrow reserve in a patient aged 70-79
PFS benefit only; OS immature at primary report (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.44-1.11)

picks.rationale: She is already on bevacizumab, and continuing it is the lowest-disruption maintenance choice with the deepest safety track record (GOG-218 and ICON7 both reported in 2011, and the AE profile has been mapped ever since). Neither named veto applies here: no neuropathy, no marrow suppression. The PFS gain is real but modest (HR 0.717, 95% CI 0.625-0.824 in GOG-218; OS not improved overall), and the operative worry is hers specifically: G2+ hypertension ran 22.9% in the bev-throughout arm, and with a high VTE history plus a prior IVC filter, bleeding and thrombosis need active management. I rank it as the safe continuation, not the high-efficacy play.
primary_concerns: High VTE history plus prior IVC filter against bevacizumab's thrombotic and bleeding class effect
G2+ hypertension 22.9% requiring therapy; needs ongoing BP monitoring
PFS-only benefit, with no OS improvement in the overall GOG-218 population

picks.rationale: For a patient aged 70-79 who wants an oral, low-burden option, letrozole is the gentlest thing on the list: aromatase-inhibitor toxicity is arthralgia and slow bone-density loss, the class has decades of post-marketing data from breast cancer, and none of her vetoes are in play. Her tumor is ER-positive at ~80% of nuclei, which gives a real rationale, though PR-negativity tempers the expected size of any benefit. Be honest about the evidence: this is a tier-4 retrospective letrozole-maintenance series (60% vs 38.5% RFS at 24 months, p=0.035), not a randomized trial, so I hold it at low confidence. It earns its place on tolerability, not on the strength of the efficacy data.
primary_concerns: Evidence is tier-4 retrospective, not randomized
PR-negativity tempers expected magnitude despite strong ER positivity
Likely lower absolute efficacy than PARP or bevacizumab maintenance

picks.rationale: Rucaparib is the other all-comer 1L PARP maintenance option, with an ITT PFS HR of 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68) in ATHENA-MONO and benefit that held in the HRD-negative subgroup, so a BRCA-WT, GIS-unquantified tumor still qualifies. It sits behind niraparib for me on two counts: it triggers the same myelosuppression veto (G3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6%), and it adds G3+ transaminase elevation in 10.6%, which matters more here because her baseline bilirubin is 1.5. The transaminitis is usually transient and her ALT/AST are normal at baseline, so it is watchable rather than disqualifying. Reasonable alternative if niraparib is not tolerated, again only with serial CBC and LFT monitoring.
primary_concerns: Same severe-myelosuppression veto as niraparib (G3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6%)
G3+ transaminase elevation 10.6% against a mildly elevated baseline bilirubin of 1.5
11.8% AE-related discontinuation in ATHENA-MONO

picks.rationale: This is the highest-magnitude PARP option on paper (HRD-positive PFS HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.45; the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup HR is 0.43), and she is already on the bevacizumab backbone PAOLA-1 requires. But eligibility is contingent: the label-relevant benefit lives in HRD-positive disease defined by Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not meet that bar. Below a validated GIS >=42 she is HRD-negative and defaults to all-comer niraparib. I rank it last and strictly conditional, because the combination ran G3+ AEs around 57% (hypertension 19%, anemia 17%), and the bevacizumab-driven hypertension and VTE/bleeding risk compound her thrombotic history.
primary_concerns: Eligibility contingent on a validated MyChoice GIS >=42 the patient does not yet have
Combination G3+ AE ~57%; hypertension 19% and anemia 17% touch both the VTE caution and the myelosuppression veto
Highest toxicity burden of the maintenance options

notes: The rank-1 shared workup is still diagnostic, not therapeutic: order a validated genomic-instability assay (Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS or equivalent) to settle olaparib-plus-bevacizumab eligibility, and a confirmatory HER2 re-stain, since the IHC 1+ rests on a single surgical-path specimen and Altera could not evaluate HER2. Four options I did not rank, each with the specific reason. Disitamab vedotin is out outright: its MMAE payload caused 68.2% any-grade and 18.7% G3+ peripheral neuropathy plus 12.1% G3+ neutropenia (pmid 37988648), which hits both named vetoes with no mitigation on offer. T-DXd I leave unranked for ovarian IHC 1+: the missing datum is any ovarian efficacy or safety at this expression tier (DESTINY-PanTumor02 enrolled 2+/3+, the tumor-agnostic approval needs 3+), and its adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis of 10.5-12.1% with fatal cases is an IV, uncharacterized long-tail risk in exactly this population. The PI3K/AKT row is tier-5 context only, with no approved HGSOC therapy and no per-term AE data for PIK3CA-amplified disease. GEN-1/IMNN-001 is regimen-matched and she is already on it, but the public topline carries no per-term G3+ AE table, so I cannot underwrite its safety as a ranked maintenance pick yet.

picks.rationale: PRIMA is the cleanest evidence in the file: a 2:1 randomized double-blind phase 3 (n=733) with a pre-specified PFS hit in the all-comer population, HR 0.62 (0.50-0.76, p<0.001), RoB2 low, NEJM. All-comer enrollment is the point. She qualifies without a BRCA mutation or a validated HRD score, so the rank-1 claim does not lean on a subgroup. Two honest caveats: PFS is a surrogate and OS was immature at the primary report (HR 0.70, 0.44-1.11, crossing 1), and grade 3+ thrombocytopenia (28.7%) and anemia (31%) run into her myelosuppression veto.
primary_concerns: Surrogate primary endpoint (PFS); OS immature at primary report with CI crossing 1
Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% collide with the severe-myelosuppression veto
HRD-positive subgroup HR 0.43 is larger but is a subgroup; the overall-population estimand is what applies here

picks.rationale: ATHENA-MONO replicates the all-comer PARP-maintenance signal in a separate phase 3 (n=538, 4:1): pre-specified ITT PFS HR 0.52 (0.40-0.68, p<0.0001), RoB2 low, JCO. Two independent registered trials hitting the same endpoint is what actually moves me on this class for a BRCA-WT tumor, and the benefit holds in the ITT and HRD-negative strata rather than only a BRCA subgroup. The surrogate-endpoint and myelosuppression caveats from niraparib carry over (grade 3+ anemia 28.7%).
primary_concerns: Surrogate primary endpoint (PFS); no mature OS in the primary report
Grade 3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6% against the myelosuppression veto
ALT/AST elevation 10.6% (usually transient; her baseline LFTs are normal)

picks.rationale: Replicated across two phase 3 trials she matches on indication (GOG-218 HR 0.717, 0.625-0.824; ICON7 HR 0.81, 0.70-0.94), and she is already on the backbone. The hard limit is that this is PFS only. GOG-218 found no OS benefit in the overall population, and ICON7's OS gain sat in a high-risk subgroup, which is a subgroup result from an open-label trial (RoB2 some-concern). VTE and bleeding risk is the operative safety problem given her VTE history and prior IVC filter.
primary_concerns: PFS-only benefit; no OS gain in the GOG-218 overall population
ICON7 OS benefit is a high-risk subgroup finding, and ICON7 was open-label (RoB2 some-concern: outcome ascertainment)
VTE and bleeding risk against her VTE history and prior IVC filter

picks.rationale: PAOLA-1 is RoB2 low, but the headline HR 0.33 is the HRD-positive subgroup, defined by MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and she has neither. Her qualitative Altera instability call does not clear that companion-diagnostic bar, so on today's data she falls into the ITT estimand (HR 0.59, 0.49-0.72) or defaults to HRD-negative. I put it below the all-comer PARPs precisely because the impressive number is subgroup-derived and contingent on a validated GIS she has not had. Bevacizumab toxicity also stacks on PARP myelosuppression.
primary_concerns: The label-relevant HR 0.33 is a subgroup estimand she does not yet qualify for; ITT HR is 0.59
Eligibility contingent on a validated GIS (MyChoice >=42) she has not had; qualitative Altera call does not meet it
Combination grade 3+ AE ~57%; hypertension 19% plus PARP anemia 17%, stacking bev VTE/bleeding risk on myelosuppression

picks.rationale: For ovarian HER2-low IHC 1+ there is no direct efficacy evidence. The ovarian datapoint (PanTumor02, ORR 45%, n=40) enrolled IHC 2+/3+, not 1+, and is single-arm on a response-rate surrogate; the tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+. The IHC 1+ efficacy that exists is breast (DESTINY-Breast04 PFS HR 0.51; Breast06 HR 0.62), so the case for her tumor is cross-tumor extrapolation standing in for indication data. Layer on a single-specimen HER2 call (Altera could not stain HER2) and 10-12% ILD, and this is an investigational future-relapse option, not a maintenance pick I can support now.
primary_concerns: No ovarian HER2-low IHC 1+ efficacy data; the case rests on cross-tumor extrapolation from breast plus the DXd bystander mechanism (preclinical)
Ovarian evidence (PanTumor02) is single-arm, ORR surrogate, n=40, and enrolled IHC 2+/3+ above her tier; tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+
HER2 1+ rests on a single surgical-path IHC (Altera could not evaluate HER2); a confirmatory re-stain is needed before acting
ILD/pneumonitis 10-12% including fatal cases

notes: Why some options stayed off the ranked list. Disitamab vedotin: the only HER2-low efficacy read is an ESMO 2024 abstract (ORR ~34%) in PAM-pathway-selected breast, and the MMAE payload runs 68% any-grade and 18.7% grade 3+ peripheral neuropathy plus neutropenia, hitting both her named vetoes; abstract-only and veto-incompatible keeps it off. Letrozole looks attractive as an oral low-burden option, but the supporting study is a retrospective non-randomized comparison nested in a translational paper (ROBINS-I serious), not the single-arm phase 2 the trials row implied. GEN-1/IMNN-001 is the program she is already on, but the efficacy is sponsor topline plus an abstract (PFS HR 0.79, no CI, no p-value, no peer-reviewed full text), so it is not citable at RCT grade yet. The PI3K and MAP2K4 baskets have no ovarian efficacy estimand at all. Two workup asks would change the ranking: a validated GIS (MyChoice >=42) would move PAOLA-1 up, and a confirmatory HER2 re-stain would harden the single-specimen 1+ call before anyone acts on the HER2 axis.

picks.rationale: PRIMA enrolled all-comers and still cut progression risk at HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76); in genomically unstable disease like hers the HRD-positive subgroup ran HR 0.43, and that is the upside I am betting on without waiting for a GIS score. The preclinical pharmacology points straight at her genotype: niraparib partitions into tumor at roughly 16-fold higher dose-normalized exposure than olaparib and shrank a BRCA-wild-type PDX by 58% (pmid:30647846), the BRCA-proficient setting she sits in. It is oral, which she wants. The honest catch is myelosuppression at 31% grade 3+ anemia and 28.7% thrombocytopenia, which bumps her veto, so I would start at the individualized weight/platelet dose and watch her baseline WBC of 3.5.
primary_concerns: Myelosuppression is a named veto and niraparib delivers it; her baseline WBC of 3.5 leaves little headroom even with individualized dosing.
The all-comer HR 0.62 is solid, but the larger 0.43 benefit is a subgroup bet, not a guarantee for her unscored tumor.

picks.rationale: This is the biggest number on the board, HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.25-0.45) with mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 months in HRD-positive disease, and she is already running the bevacizumab backbone it needs. The bet: send a validated MyChoice GIS, and given her documented chromosomal instability I expect it to clear 42, which opens PAOLA-1 and the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive HR of 0.43. Preclinical work shows anti-angiogenics manufacture an HR defect in BRCA-proficient cells and sensitize them to PARP trapping (pmid:31092693), so the combination has a real reason to work in her exact genotype. Two toxicities stack, PARP myelosuppression and bevacizumab VTE/bleeding against her prior IVC filter, though the bev risk is one she is already carrying.
primary_concerns: The whole case rests on a MyChoice GIS that has not been run; come back under 42 and she is HRD-negative, dropping this to the ITT HR 0.59.
Layering PARP marrow toxicity onto bevacizumab clotting and bleeding risk in a woman with a prior IVC filter is the combination I worry about most.

picks.rationale: Here is my long shot, held for relapse: treat an HER2-low ovarian tumor the way HER2-low breast gets treated, where T-DXd posted a PFS HR of 0.51 (95% CI 0.40-0.64) in the hormone-receptor-positive subgroup that mirrors her ER-positive biology (pmid:35665782), with Breast06 holding the signal down to ultralow at HR 0.62. The mechanism travels: freed DXd kills HER2-low and neighboring cells by bystander effect, shown in ovarian and uterine carcinosarcoma in vivo (pmid:36610380). The thin part is real, since she is IHC 1+, under the 2+/3+ ovarian cohort that hit 45% ORR and under the IHC 3+ tumor-agnostic approval, so this is investigational off a single stain I would re-confirm first. None of her named vetoes fire; the cost of entry is IV dosing and a 10-12% ILD rate that has been fatal, so lung monitoring is not optional.
primary_concerns: IHC 1+ sits below every threshold that carries actual ovarian efficacy data, so this is extrapolation resting on one specimen.
ILD at 10-12% with fatal cases, plus IV against her oral preference; this is a relapse option, not something to launch in remission.

picks.rationale: She is already on it and responding, with R0, CA-125 normalized, and ctDNA undetectable, so continuing the IL-12 immunogene is the low-regret piece of an aggressive plan. The topline reads HR 0.79 for PFS and, the part that interests me, HR 0.69 for OS with about a 13-month median OS gain (OVATION 2, nct:NCT03393884), and the IL-12 route works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment rather than the MSI/TMB checkpoint axis her MSS, TMB-low tumor forecloses. The evidence is early-phase and the OS curve is immature, so I hold this loosely. It is well tolerated by IP delivery, trips none of her vetoes, and she prefers trials.
primary_concerns: Efficacy is sponsor topline from an early-phase trial with immature OS and no published CI, so the 0.69 could soften.
It is already her current therapy, so ranking it mostly argues against abandoning a working regimen rather than adding new ground.

notes: Rejected disitamab vedotin (NCT06003231 / NCT06660511) outright despite it being the only HER2 option that formally accepts IHC 1+ ovarian: its MMAE payload runs 68% any-grade peripheral neuropathy, 18.7% grade 3+, plus neutropenia (pmid:37988648), hitting both of her named vetoes head-on. That is the harm line I will not cross, even with my efficacy prior. Dropped letrozole as too low-magnitude for my weighting despite clean tolerability and 80% ER positivity, and olaparib monotherapy (SOLO1) is foreclosed by BRCA wild-type status.
